To whom it may concern:
I am writing, in a dictated letter that I may not have fully read, in support of the request for magnetic resonance imaging of the right ankle for my patient Mrs. Bright. She is a sixty three year old woman who sprained the ankle on the 13th of January and was seen in our emergency department on January 14; plain films showed no fracture. One week later, which is today, she is still unable to walk without the boot or crutches, there is swelling and tenderness over the lateral ligaments and pain with weight bearing, and I am concerned about an occult osteochondral injury or a high grade ligament tear, particularly because she has obesity and prediabetes, which slow healing.
She has no history of previous ankle surgery. I would like to emphasise that she lives alone for part of the week while her husband Lyle works away; the nearest relative is her daughter Dawn Bright-Okoro, who will accompany her. The patient is not employed so I cannot give work restrictions. Please reach me on my direct line 319-555-0165 or the office (319) 555-0100 ext 4271. Patient portal reference https://my.prairieline.example/pt/mbright2028.
Sincerely,
Henrietta Oyelowo-Kane, MD Internal Medicine NPI 1558820477 M.A.B. file; cc: Mrs. Bright
